captured_note: The inventory (docs/INVENTORY.md) classifies VAR as submodule+adapter, MIT.
note: The model is the pinned upstream under third_party/var, imported and never copied here (DESIGN section 1). Pinned DIRECTLY, no fork: VAR's model runs on a CPU or a GPU unmodified -- it has no hardcoded device (the only torch.cuda.amp.autocast on the model path is enabled=False, a no-op on a CPU) -- so it needs no patch. This is DESIGN's submodule+adapter case, unlike mar, whose model forced a submodule+patch fork. The upstream DDP/AMP trainer (trainer.py, dist.py, the bfloat16 autocast) is not used; train_step1_var.py owns a single-process, device-resolved loop over the model's own forward.
encoder: encoder.pt is the representation side of VAR: the token embedding (word_embed), class and positional and level embeddings, and the transformer blocks. The generative output head (head, head_nm) is excluded, so encoder.pt is the representation network. Which representation a downstream probe should read from a generative model is a separate, deferred question (CONTRACT section 7); this port ships no linear_eval stage.
rewritten_during_the_port: the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of reached through dist.py/AMP
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the cross-entropy loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)

the training loop drops the upstream DDP/AMP machinery so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged; flash/fused attention are forced off so a run does not depend on whether flash-attention is installed
